source_title: Ukrainian gets 2-year jail term for overstaying visa in Uttarakhand - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Bageshwar: A court in Uttarakhandâs Bageshwar sentenced a Ukrainian national to two years of simple imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 2 lakh for staying in India after his tourist visa expired in April 2025. The court also ordered his deportation to Ukraine after he completed his sentence. The conviction came after police found him injured in a remote village in May this year and discovered that he had no valid visa.The accused, Maxim Starchenko, a resident of Kharkiv, was convicted by chief judicial magistrate (CJM) Sandeep Kumar Tiwari on Oct 24. The order, made available on Tuesday, stated that failure to pay the fine would result in an additional six months in jail.On May 24, Kapkot police received information about an injured foreign national in Doula village. Gajendra Singh, a local, took Starchenko to the community health centre in Kapkot. Doctors later referred him to the district hospital in Bageshwar for better treatment.During questioning, Starchenko told police that he had lost his way while trekking in Bageshwar and fallen from a hilltop, sustaining injuries. However, he could not produce a valid visa.Police found that his Indian tourist visa had expired on April 16, 2025. Local Intelligence Unit also found no record of Form-C submission in his name in the district. Form-C is used to report the stay of foreign nationals at designated accommodation units.Police initiated proceedings against Starchenko under the Immigration and Foreignersâ Act.During the trial, the defence argued that Starchenko held a refugee card issued by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). It also told the court that he had stayed at an ashram in Uttarkashi and at other places.The court held that a UNHCR refugee card was not a substitute for a valid visa and convicted him on the evidence presented.Starchenko had spent four months and 28 days in jail during the trial. The court ordered that this period be adjusted against his two-year sentence and directed authorities to deport him to Ukraine after he completed his prison term, in accordance with the law.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news.
